entities.summary: Daniel Alexander Payne was an American bishop, educator, college administrator and author. A major shaper of the African Methodist Episcopal Church (AME), Payne stressed education and preparation of ministers and introduced more order in the church, becoming its sixth bishop and serving for more than four decades (1852–1893) as well as becoming one of the founders of Wilberforce University in Ohio in 1856. In 1863, the AME Church bought the college and chose Payne to lead it; he became the first African-American president of a college in the United States and served in that position until 1877.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the founders and first president of Wilberforce University, Payne played a crucial role in shaping the institution's mission to provide education to African Americans. His leadership helped establish the university as a key institution for African American higher education during the Reconstruction Era.
